demo.description: Generates a self-contained folder of deterministic example data covering all three modules (quantitative, qualitative, radiomics), with results, reproducibility receipts and a local HTML report. tools.decompressor.title: Decompress DICOM
tools.decompressor.description: Rewrite a compressed DICOM file (lossless JPEG, JPEG-LS, JPEG 2000, RLE...) uncompressed, one file per frame, in a new folder named after the file, for software that cannot read compressed DICOM.
tools.decompressor.note: The file is only read. The copies are written in Explicit VR Little Endian with the same pixels QICOM shows, in a new folder named after the file inside the folder you choose. A multi-frame file becomes one file per frame, with new instance UIDs and one new series UID; an Enhanced object stays Enhanced. Decompressing never undoes a lossy compression.
tools.decompressor.nothing_to_do: This file is already uncompressed and holds one frame: there is nothing to decompress.
tools.decompressor.will_write_one: It will become one uncompressed file.
tools.decompressor.will_write_many: It will become {count} uncompressed files, one per frame.
tools.decompressor.enhanced: Enhanced object: each file keeps its own per-frame functional group and the shared ones.
tools.decompressor.split: Each file gets its frame number as Instance Number.
tools.decompressor.lossy: The source was compressed with loss: the copies keep the same lossy pixels and say so.

tools.degradation.description: Make reproducible test images to check what a metric notices: Gaussian or Poisson noise, blur, loss of resolution, JPEG compression, one effect at a time, from one seed. The effects are saved with the result.
tools.resampling.title: Resample

tools.resampling.spacing_note: The first voxel stays in place; the step between voxels changes.
tools.resampling.reference_note: Both images must share a frame of reference (same session, or already registered): they are matched by patient coordinates, not aligned.
tools.resampling.failed: The image could not be resampled.
tools.arithmetic.title: Image arithmetic
tools.arithmetic.description: Combine images on the same grid voxel by voxel: difference, absolute difference, sum, mean of repeated acquisitions, ratio.

tools.arithmetic.spacing_warning: Same size, but a different voxel spacing: the images are not on the same grid.

tools.masks.title: Mask operations and comparison

tools.masks.note: Both masks must be on the same grid: nothing is resampled for a comparison. Choose "any label" or one value of a multi-label map.

results_table.ci_note: 95% confidence interval on the mean across the stack's slices (Student's t, using the slices as the sample). Slices of the same volume are spatially and anatomically correlated, not independent observations, so this interval is narrower - more optimistic - than a genuine independent-sample interval. Read it as a descriptive indication of how much the metric varies along the stack, not as a formal statistical inference. Empty for single 2D images, ROI rows and metrics that aggregate a volume internally: there is no per-slice sample to estimate an interval from.

background.title: Background (air)
background.optional_notice: Optional step - the analysis runs with or without it. Skip it and every metric is averaged over the whole image, air included.

background.enable_on: ✓ Air exclusion is on - click to turn it off
background.air_roi_placed_tooltip: The air sample is already placed - drag the green circle to where the air really is. Press Clear to remove it and place a new one.
background.enable_tooltip: Most pixels of a typical slice are the air around the patient, and every whole-image metric averages over them. With this on, MSE/PSNR/SSIM and the other pixel-based metrics are computed on the anatomy only; ROI measurements and SNR/CNR are never affected.
background.tolerance_tooltip: How far above the air level a pixel must be to count as anatomy, in noise spreads of the background itself. Wider excludes more.
background.threshold_tooltip: The resulting intensity threshold: at or below it is background, above it is measured. Type an exact value to set it directly.
background.disabled_hint: Off: every metric is averaged over the whole image, air included.
background.no_estimate: Load both images to detect the background.
background.summary: Air level {air_level}, threshold {threshold} - {excluded}% of the image is excluded from the whole-image metrics.
background.mostly_excluded_warning: That is nearly the whole image - check the air sample and the tolerance.
background.step_create_roi: Add the green air sample and place it on a clean background area.
background.step_place_and_detect: Position the green sample where there is only air, then press Detect air to preview the exclusion.
background.step_correct: Blue = excluded. Use Eraser to recover tissue or Air brush to exclude missed background.
background.step_erasing: Eraser on: drag over the blue area to put those pixels back into the measurement. Press Eraser again to stop.
background.step_painting: Air brush on: drag over missed background to add it to the blue excluded area. Press Air brush again to stop.
background.clear_air_rois_tooltip: Remove all air-sample ROIs from the image.
background.air_roi_tooltip: Drop the one green sampling circle on a clean patch of background, then drag it where the air really is. Only this circle estimates the air level; measurement ROIs are never used.
background.detect_tooltip: Read the air level inside the green circle and paint everything that would be left out of the metrics.
background.eraser_tooltip: Paint over the excluded (blue) area to put those pixels back into the measurement - for tissue excluded because it is as dark as air.
background.paint_air_tooltip: Paint over background the automatic detection missed to add those pixels to the excluded blue area.
background.clear_erasures_tooltip: Drop every manual brush and eraser correction and return to the detected result.
background.no_air_roi: Create the green air ROI and place it on the background first.
background.air_roi_off_slice: The green air ROI covers no pixels of the slice being analyzed - move it over the image.
background.results_note: Background air excluded: threshold {threshold}, {excluded}% of the image. Metrics without a per-pixel definition (VIF, FSIM, GMSD, MS-SSIM, HaarPSI, DISTS, LPIPS, NSS feature distance, NSS patch-distribution distance) are scored on a background-suppressed copy instead of an exactly masked one. SSIM, EPI and HFEN keep the definition they have without the mask (3D for a stack), restricted to the tissue voxels whose whole window lies inside the mask. Canonical BRISQUE and NIQE always score the whole image; ROI and background exclusion do not apply.

qualitative_privacy.dialog_title: These images are de-identified for you
qualitative_privacy.dialog_body:
When you save this evaluation, QICOM writes a de-identified copy of every image into the package: DICOM files are stripped of patient identity following the PS3.15 Basic Profile, and NIfTI files have their free-text header fields cleared. A DICOM file that cannot be proven safe to share stops the save rather than leaving in silence: QICOM then asks whether to export it anyway, and if you agree it is marked as not verified.

Your own files on disk are never modified. File names are copied as they are, so rename any file whose name identifies a patient.

about.title: About QICOM
about.designed_in: Designed and developed in Lugano, Switzerland.
about.summary: QICOM compares medical images and quantifies their quality: objective metrics with ROIs and difference maps, blinded structured reader evaluations, and paired radiomics with repeatability statistics.
about.field.author: Author
about.intended_use.heading: Intended use
about.intended_use.body: QICOM is intended for research and quality-assessment use only. It is not a medical device, and it is not intended for clinical diagnosis or for any decision concerning the care of a patient.
about.intended_use.detail: The numbers QICOM produces describe images, not patients. Deciding whether a given comparison is meaningful, and interpreting its result, remains the responsibility of the qualified user who set it up.
about.scope.does_items:
Computes full-reference metrics between a reference image and one or more comparison images (MSE, MAE, RMSE, NMSE, PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, FSIM, GMSD, HaarPSI, VIF, LPIPS, DISTS).
Computes no-reference quality indices and ROI statistics (NSS feature distance, NSS patch-distribution distance, sharpness, edge preservation, SNR, CNR, CV).
Displays difference heatmaps with standard medical LUTs, line profiles and per-slice distributions.
Runs blinded, structured qualitative evaluations and aggregates the answers of several readers.
Extracts paired 2D/3D radiomic features, with delta-radiomics and ICC/CCC repeatability statistics.
Exports results to Excel and keeps projects in a local database.
NSS feature distance and NSS patch-distribution distance retain their own reference-model scales. The additional BRISQUE and NIQE scores use separately identified pretrained models.
about.scope.does_not_items:
It does not register, align or resample images onto each other for the quantitative metrics: it compares them element by element, as loaded.
It does not diagnose, does not detect findings, and supports no decision concerning a patient.
It implements no DICOM network or storage service and claims no conformance to the DICOM Standard.
It sends nothing anywhere: no telemetry, no cloud processing, no automatic updates.
about.registration.heading: Spatial correspondence
about.registration.body: QICOM compares images element by element and never registers them. Every reference-based metric (MSE, MAE, RMSE, PSNR, SSIM and the others) therefore assumes that the two inputs already correspond spatially. QICOM reports the mismatches it can read from the DICOM headers - photometric interpretation, pixel spacing, orientation, slice spacing - but it cannot detect a misalignment the headers do not describe.
about.ibsi.heading: IBSI status
about.ibsi.body: The radiomics module targets the IBSI reference definitions and applies the IBSI convention where PyRadiomics differs from it, but it is not IBSI certified: IBSI operates no certification scheme. See the validation documentation for the benchmark results feature by feature.
about.legal.warranty: Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, this software is distributed on an "AS IS" basis, without warranties or conditions of any kind, either express or implied. See the LICENSE file for the exact terms.
about.legal.third_party: QICOM is distributed with third-party components that remain under their own licenses; their notices are collected in {file}.
about.privacy.heading: Local processing
about.privacy.local: QICOM performs all image processing locally on the machine it runs on. It transmits no image data, embeds no telemetry and makes no network connection during an analysis.
about.privacy.network_exception: QICOM opens network connections only when you start them explicitly, and no analysis ever triggers one: the download of the optional learned-metric checkpoints, and the download of the official IBSI reference resources for the IBSI verification. Every downloaded file is verified against a known SHA-256 and size.
about.privacy.dicom_handling: DICOM metadata is read from the files you open and stays in your local project. Portable exports are de-identified by default, with UID consistency preserved; SECURITY.md states the exact guarantees and their documented limits.
about.privacy.no_telemetry: QICOM collects no usage statistics and checks for no updates. Projects, logs and the local database stay on this machine and are not encrypted at rest: use the operating system's disk encryption and access controls when they hold sensitive data.
about.citation.intro: If QICOM contributed to work you publish, please cite it as:

llm_export.title: QICOM — export for AI-assisted reading
llm_export.instructions_body: QICOM is an offline application that measures image quality on medical images; it produced the numbers below and did not interpret them. The metric definitions in this document are authoritative: prefer them over your own knowledge of metrics that happen to share a name, because the exact formula, normalization and sign convention differ between tools. Answer in the language of this document. Where a value is marked as not computed, say so plainly instead of estimating it. Do not give a diagnostic or clinical judgement, and do not infer patient, study or equipment details: none are present here.
llm_export.disclaimer_body: These are image-quality measurements, not a clinical assessment, and they do not establish that any image is fit or unfit for diagnostic use. Any explanation an AI model produces from this file is unvalidated and may be wrong. Check anything that matters against the QICOM documentation and a qualified physicist or clinician.
llm_export.direction_target: closest to the target is better
llm_export.row_budget_note: This export lists {emitted} of {total} result rows; {omitted} were omitted to keep the file small enough to paste into a chat. The rows shown were selected deterministically, one per metric in turn, so every metric in the analysis appears at least once. The provenance digest below covers the complete result set, not this excerpt - a report built from the same analysis always shows the same rows.
llm_export.provenance_line: QICOM {version} · calculation schema v{calculation_schema} · export schema v{export_schema} · exported results SHA-256 {digest}
export_summary.include_llm_report.toolti: Also write a single Markdown file carrying each metric's value and its definition, so an AI chat assistant can explain the results. QICOM performs no AI processing and sends nothing anywhere; it only writes the file.
llm_export.upload_warning_body: QICOM has written a Markdown file containing your metric values and their definitions. It deliberately excludes file names, image headers, patient identifiers and any machine details. QICOM does not upload it and contacts no AI service. Once you send it somewhere yourself it leaves QICOM's control, so read it first and follow your institution's rules on where results may be sent.
llm_export.citation_body: If your answer, or any text you help write from this file, is used in a paper, report or presentation, that work must cite QICOM, the software that produced these measurements, with the reference below. When you write text intended for publication, include this reference in its reference list exactly as given, without rewording it.
llm_export.citation_riqe: These results include RIQE scores, so the work must also cite the RIQE study and its model release:
llm_export.citation_riqe_inherited: The RIQE model is distributed under CC BY 4.0, whose attribution terms also require citing the data it was fitted on, the archive holding them and the algorithm it implements, and acknowledging the grants {acknowledgement}:
